Independent bounded feasibility check: enumerate relevant masks at 3x4 and 3x6, retaining masks with n|R|<=m|N(R)| for every row subset R in the allowed bipartite graph. Compare integer mnG with the two sharp degree caps. At 3x4 the sparse feasible masks comprise 72 matchings and 210 strict degree gaps; at 3x6 they comprise 228 matchings and 753 strict gaps, and the divisible cases include 180 biregular masks and 15480 strict degree gaps.
correctness.rationale: For B the indicator of the forbidden cells, double-centering gives the orthogonal projection PB because the discarded row/column effects pair to zero with all zero-margin matrices. Each feasible X satisfies <X-U,PB>=-k/(mn). Thus feasibility implies PB is nonzero, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives the degree bound. Its denominator comes from <PB,B>=k-sum(r_i^2)/n-sum(c_j^2)/m+k^2/(mn). For k at most min(m,n), each degree square sum is at least k, with simultaneous equality precisely for a matching. In that case every (PB)_ij on the mask is D/(mn), where D=(m-1)(n-1)+k-1. The candidate U-PB/D has zero forbidden entries, correct margins, and off-mask entries with numerators mn, n(m-1), m(n-1), or mn-m-n over mnD, all nonnegative. It is an equality case of Cauchy–Schwarz, proving attainment; strictness for every other feasible mask follows from the degree bound. For the divisible case, alternatively use ||X-U||_F^2=||X||_F^2-1/(mn) and apply Cauchy–Schwarz to the mn-k allowed cells of total mass one. Equality forces constant mass there, which has the required margins exactly when the mask is biregular. Its existence follows by giving each row a consecutive block of k/m distinct residues from the sequence 0 through k-1 modulo n; whole residue cycles give k/n in each column. These arguments address uniqueness and all claimed endpoints. The frozen line 60 calls the 941 optional cases nonmatching, but the script counts all feasible iterations, including matching and singleton masks, and may sample duplicates. That changes neither theorem nor equality proof.
residual_risks: The finite check certifies degree inequalities on enumerated feasible masks, not distances via numerical optimization or the unrestricted theorem. The theorem asserts no optimizer at arbitrary intermediate k or for nonuniform margins.

value.rationale: The center-to-face distance is a natural Euclidean invariant for a fixed number of imposed zeros. The exact classification resolves whether collisions of forbidden positions can ever make the nearest face closer in the sparse regime, and quantifies the trade-off through degree dispersion. The attained bound distinguishes separated sparse masks from balanced dense ones and is more informative than a per-mask optimization routine.
residual_risks: No unproved extension to all cardinalities, nonuniform margins, or practical transport optimization is credited.
